title: 'Integrate now' silently threw away 8 of 9 subs and presented the 1-frame result as a finished master, with no error, warning or count anywhere in the UI
what_happened: With 9 accepted 300s subs, clicking 'Integrate now' produced a master card reading 'M51 - L / 1 frame - 00:05:00 integration - L' and no other feedback: no toast, no error banner, no 'x of y subs rejected' line. The database shows integrated_master_frames has 1 accepted row and 8 rows with rejection_reason 'registration failed: too few stars to register: reference=0, frame=N, need >= 3', and integrated_masters.stats_json is {"framesIntegrated":1,"framesRejected":8,...}. Two distinct failures compound: (a) the integrator picked sub 1 as the alignment reference, detected 0 stars in it, and then failed every other sub against that empty reference instead of choosing a different reference or aborting; (b) the count of dropped subs exists in the outcome and in the DB but is never rendered for a manual integration.
expected: Two things. (1) A reference frame with 0 detected stars must not be accepted as the reference -- fall back to the next-best frame (frames 4-9 each detected 29-30 stars) or abort with 'could not find a usable reference frame'. (2) Integration must report its own result: 'Integrated 1 of 9 subs - 8 failed to register' with the reason, exactly as the automatic-integration path already does (auto_integration_service.dart:378 builds precisely that sentence). Losing 89% of a night's data must never be silent.
repro: 1. Seed 10 lights for one session with real FITS star fields (star sigma 1.0-2.25 px). 2. Analytics > History > Audit Night A > sparkles. 3. Workbench > 'Reject HFR above' at 3.5 (leaves 9 accepted). 4. Scroll the right column to Integration settings, click 'Integrate now'. 5. Wait ~40 s. 6. Read the Masters card and look for any error surface.
evidence: UI after the run: Masters card 'M51 - L / 1 frame - 00:05:00 integration - L' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-24.png), header still '9 accepted - 1 rejected', no toast (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-21.png). DB: sqlite3 skotiq.db "select image_id,accepted,rejection_reason from integrated_master_frames where master_id=2" -> 1|1|(null) then 8 rows 0|'registration failed: too few stars to register: reference=0, frame=4..30, need >= 3'. stats_json {"framesIntegrated":1,"framesRejected":8}. App log: '[STAR_DETECT] Detected 0 stars after filtering' on the reference frame.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:710 integrate() -- the returned outcome is stored in state.lastOutcome but workbench_view.dart:190 uses it only for a preview path and a button label; framesIntegrated/framesRejected are never rendered. Reference selection is in the native post-session integration path.
proposed_fix: In integrate(), after the outcome returns, if outcome.result.framesRejected > 0 raise a warning toast + a persistent banner on the master card carrying the count and the most common rejection_reason; reuse auto_integration_service.dart's existing summary builder. Separately, make reference selection reject a candidate with fewer than the minimum registrable stars and retry with the next candidate before failing the run.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end. I restored session 1 to the finding's exact state (header '9 accepted · 1 rejected', panel 'Will integrate 9 accepted subs using Winsorized sigma') and pressed Integrate now. Result: master id 14 with stats_json {"framesIntegrated":1,"framesRejected":8,"rmsResidual":0.0,"totalIntegrationSec":300.0} and 8 integrated_master_frames rows reading 'registration failed: too few stars to register: reference=0, frame=4|11|29|30, need >= 3'. UI afterwards: Masters card 'M51 · L / 1 frame · 00:05:00 integration · L', header still '9 accepted · 1 rejected', and the entire accessibility tree contains no error, warning or rejected-count node for that run. Cause is nailed down further than the finding states: the reference is audit_L_001.fits, the sub with the brightest near-saturated star (57952 ADU), which the app's detector scores 0 stars on while my independent peak finder reads 40 well-separated stars; with that sub culled the same button integrates 7 of 7 at 0.11 px residual. Reporting half verified structurally: session_review_controller.dart:710 integrate() is exact; workbench_view.dart:190 'final outcome = state.lastOutcome' is exact and consumed only at :193 for previewPath; MasterPreviewView.fromOutcome (master_preview_view.dart:33-42) is the ONLY widget rendering '${r.framesIntegrated} frames · ${r.framesRejected} rejected' and its sole caller is ab_compare_panel.dart:284, while the workbench master card at workbench_view.dart:353 uses MasterPreviewView.fromMaster whose stat line has no rejected term.

title: Project-growth panel groups subs by UTC calendar day, so one continuous evening is reported as two nights and every night is dated a day late
what_happened: Session Review (narrative) 'This project over time' reports '2.0h integrated - 24 frames across 4 nights' with x-axis labels Jul 26 / Jul 28 / Jul 29 / Jul 30, and 'Best night: Jul 28 - 0.5h'. The database contains exactly THREE observing sessions (Audit Night A on the evening of Jul 25 local, B on Jul 27 local, C on Jul 29 local). Audit Night C is one continuous 50-minute run (19:30-20:20 America/New_York) that straddles 00:00 UTC, and the panel splits it into two separate 'nights' (Jul 29 with 4 frames, Jul 30 with 4 frames). Every other night is also labelled with the following calendar day because 21:00 EDT is 01:00 UTC.
expected: Nights should be grouped by OBSERVING night in the site's local time (the conventional noon-to-noon boundary), so three sessions produce three points labelled Jul 25, Jul 27, Jul 29 and the panel says '3 nights'. Never a UTC calendar day: for any observer west of Greenwich the label is a day late, and for any observer east of Greenwich (all of Europe/Asia) the 00:00 UTC boundary falls in the MIDDLE of the observing night, splitting every single night in two.
repro: 1. Seed three sessions of M51 lights, the third spanning 19:30-20:20 America/New_York on 2026-07-29 (crosses 00:00 UTC). 2. Analytics > History > Audit Night A > sparkles (Review & Integrate). 3. Scroll the narrative view to 'This project over time'.
evidence: UI: '2.0h integrated - 24 frames across 4 nights', axis Jul 26 / Jul 28 / Jul 29 / Jul 30, 'Best night: Jul 28 - 0.5h' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-08.png). DB: sqlite3 skotiq.db "select strftime('%Y-%m-%d',captured_at,'unixepoch') utc, strftime('%Y-%m-%d',captured_at,'unixepoch','localtime') local, count(*) from captured_images group by 1" -> 2026-07-26|2026-07-25|10, 2026-07-28|2026-07-27|6, 2026-07-29|2026-07-29|4, 2026-07-30|2026-07-29|4. Three local nights, four UTC days.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/smart_project_service.dart:679 _dayOf() -> DateTime.utc(dt.year, dt.month, dt.day); used by growthCurve(), bestNight() and reReferenceAdvice()
proposed_fix: Group by observing night, not UTC date: shift the timestamp by the site's UTC offset and then by -12h before truncating to a day (the standard 'noon-to-noon' night key), and label the point with that local date. bestNight() and reReferenceAdvice() share _dayOf and are wrong in the same way -- a European user's 'best night' is currently the better HALF of a night.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim in the running app. Session Review > Narrative > 'This project over time' renders '2.0h integrated · 24 frames across 4 nights', 'Best night: Jul 28 · 0.5h', axis Jul 26 / Jul 28 / Jul 29 / Jul 30. Ground truth from the DB: three observing sessions (Audit Night A 2026-07-25 21:00, B 2026-07-27 21:00, C 2026-07-29 19:30 local America/New_York); master 1's 24 accepted subs group as 2026-07-26|10, 2026-07-28|6, 2026-07-29|4, 2026-07-30|4 by UTC day but 2026-07-25|10, 2026-07-27|6, 2026-07-29|8 by local day. Audit Night C is one continuous 19:30-20:20 local run and 20:00 EDT is exactly 00:00 UTC, so it is cut in half. I also saw the day-late half in isolation earlier: with a single-night master the panel read '1 frame across 1 night' labelled 'Jul 26' for a session whose header reads '2026-07-25 21:00'. Cited location exact: smart_project_service.dart:679 _dayOf returns DateTime.utc(dt.year, dt.month, dt.day); its one call site is :583 in _foldedSubs (captureDate), feeding growthCurve (:279-287) and _meanWeightByNight (:606-607) behind bestNight (:318). The finding also names reReferenceAdvice (:341); it shares _foldedSubs but I did not verify it consumes captureDate, so treat that third consumer as unconfirmed.

title: Narrowband mixer 'Apply palette' is a dead control: no composite, no file, no error, no log line
what_happened: With three finalized single-filter masters for the target (Ha 20 frames, OIII 15, SII 10), the Narrowband mixer renders correctly, SHO/HOO presets populate the weight matrix correctly, and 'Apply palette' is enabled. Pressing it five times (three via click-img, twice via a raw xdotool click on the hovered button) produced nothing at all: narrowband_composites stayed at 0 rows, no FITS was written anywhere on disk, no toast appeared in the accessibility tree on six consecutive polls, and the app log recorded no combine activity. The screen's toast path is demonstrably alive -- the same session surfaced 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling' from the cull rail -- and the neighbouring 'Run both' A/B button responded immediately with a 'Preview...' state and native STAR_DETECT log lines, so neither the toast machinery nor the click mapping explains the silence.
expected: Apply palette should either produce a narrowband_composites row plus an on-disk composite FITS and render it in the composite card, or fail loudly with the reason ('Need at least two finalized narrowband masters to combine.' is already written for that case). Silently doing nothing on the mixer's only action makes the whole SHO/HOO feature untestable by the user.
repro: 1. Seed three finalized integrated_masters for the target with filter Ha / OIII / SII and real master_fits_path files. 2. Session Review > Workbench > Refresh. 3. Scroll to 'Narrowband mixer', press SHO (matrix fills SII->R, Ha->G, OIII->B correctly). 4. Press 'Apply palette'. 5. sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select count(*) from narrowband_composites' -> 0; no new .fits under the masters output dir; no toast.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-30.png (mixer with 3 channels), rsr-33.png (SHO matrix + enabled Apply palette), rsr-35.png (cursor hovering the button, confirming the hit target). AT-SPI polls immediately after the click contain only 'panel: Combine matrix' -- no error node. DB: narrowband_composites count 0 after 5 presses. Log tail contains nothing between the click and the next discovery sweep.
proposed_fix: Instrument runNarrowband with an entry log and surface every exit path (including the <2-input guard) through the same toast the cull rail uses; then fix whichever leg is swallowing the call. The button should also show a busy state while combiningNarrowband is true, which would have made the no-op visible.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with a control experiment that rules out the obvious false-positive explanations. Four presses of 'Apply palette' (including one clicked dead-centre after re-measuring from a fresh screenshot, because an A/B progress bar had shifted the layout) produced: narrowband_composites still 0 rows, no new .fits under the masters output dir, no error/composite node in the accessibility tree over six consecutive polls, no toast in a screenshot taken 1.0 s after the click, nothing in the app log. Click mapping proven good: a click 120 px below the same button, on 'Run both', fired immediately and produced 15+ native '[STAR_DETECT] ... Detected 29 stars' lines plus a visible 'Preview... 100%' bar. Preconditions satisfied: three finalized masters (Ha 20 / OIII 15 / SII 10) with on-disk master_fits_path files, and NarrowbandChannelRef.fitsPath comes straight from m.masterFitsPath (controller :366-370), so runNarrowband's 'inputs.length < 2' early-out with its error toast cannot fire. Cited chain matches source with small drift: workbench_view.dart:304 exact, runNarrowband declared at :1233, combineChannels at post_session_seam.dart:326-333 (finding says :327). CAVEAT: I could not pin which link is broken — the button's onPressed never invoking onApply, or bridge.apiCombineChannels never returning (invisible because SkotiqButton here is built without isLoading, so combiningNarrowband:true shows no spinner). Dart-side logging does not reach app.log in this build, so log silence does not discriminate. Do not fix one link on faith.

title: Stack & Share byte-swaps every pixel when 'Apply calibration' is on (the default), so it reports 'Reference frame has only 0 stars' and cannot stack anything
what_happened: With 8 accepted 300s L subs whose FITS provably contain 40 well-separated stars each (peak 40614 ADU over a 440 ADU background, sigma 22 ADU -> SNR ~1800), pressing Start in Stack & Share fails instantly with 'Failed to initialize stacker: Reference frame has only 0 stars, need at least 5 for alignment'. Turning OFF the 'Apply calibration' switch and pressing Start again on the SAME frames initialises fine -- the log reads 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars'. The two paths differ only in how the pixels reach the stacker: calibration-off uses the native file loader (stacking_start_from_file), calibration-on loads the frame into Dart via apiReadFitsLinearData and hands back a u16 buffer (stacking_start_from_data). The bridge's image_data_to_linear_f64 decodes the ImageData buffer with u16::from_be_bytes, but fits.rs wrote that buffer with to_le_bytes (as does every other reader in the imaging crate -- processing.rs, calibration.rs, registration.rs, stretch.rs, star_reduction.rs, background_extraction.rs and lib.rs all use from_le_bytes). Every pixel therefore comes back byte-swapped: a 440 ADU background becomes 0xB801 = 47105 and a 40614 ADU star becomes 0xA69E = 42654, so the background spans ~42000-52000 with ~10000 ADU of fake noise and the stars are buried. Hence zero detections. 'Apply calibration' is ON by default, so out of the box Stack & Share fails 100% of the time on 16-bit FITS -- the format every camera writes.
expected: apiReadFitsLinearData must decode ImageData with the same endianness fits.rs encoded it with (little-endian). Stack & Share with the default options must stack the session's frames.
repro: 1. Have a session with 8 accepted 16-bit (BITPIX=16, BZERO=32768) light FITS. 2. Imaging > Stack > Stack & Share. 3. Leave all options at their defaults and press Start -> 'Reference frame has only 0 stars'. 4. Toggle 'Apply calibration' OFF and press Start -> stacker initialises with 34 stars (it then fails later for an unrelated reason, see the residual finding). 5. Verify the frames really have stars: python3 peak-finder over audit_L_017..024.fits reports 40 local maxima each, top fluxes ~37000-40000 over a 440 median with sigma 22.
evidence: UI: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-09.png shows 'Apply calibration' ON with 'Stack & Share failed / SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Failed to initialize stacker: Reference frame has only 0 stars, need at least 5 for alignment)'; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-10.png shows the same dialog with the toggle OFF. App log (/tmp/ns-audit/r-science-review/app.log): three 'Starting live stacking from data: 512x512 (262144 pixels)' entries that each ended in the 0-stars error, then '14:53:10 Starting live stacking with reference: .../audit_L_024.fits' followed by 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars'. Independent pixel check of audit_L_017.fits: median 440, MAD-sigma 22.2, 40 local maxima, brightest 40614.
where: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:1537-1560 image_data_to_linear_f64 (from_be_bytes for U16/U32/F32/F64) vs native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/fits.rs:322-365 (to_le_bytes). Reached from packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_and_share_service.dart:724 _loadRawU16 -> stacking_engine_seam.dart:172 apiReadFitsLinearData.
proposed_fix: Change the four decodes in image_data_to_linear_f64 to from_le_bytes, and add a round-trip unit test (write a known FITS, read it back through api_read_fits_linear_data, assert the pixel values match). The same bug silently corrupts two science surfaces: default_science_backend.dart:856 (the Dart fallback for per-frame science quality metrics, which then writes science_frame_quality_metrics / science_tile_metrics) and default_science_backend.dart:890-892 (computeLineRatios reads Ha/OIII/SII this way, so every BPT line ratio is computed on byte-swapped pixels), plus stretch_pipeline_service.dart:34.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live against session 3 (M51, 8 × 300 s L, BITPIX=16 BZERO=32768). Stack & Share opens with 'Apply calibration' ON; Start with untouched defaults gives 'Stack & Share failed / SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Failed to initialize stacker: Reference frame has only 0 stars, need at least 5 for alignment)' and the log shows 'Reading FITS linear data: .../audit_L_024.fits' ×2 then 'Starting live stacking from data: 512x512 (262144 pixels)'. Flipping ONLY that toggle off and pressing Start on the same 8 frames gives 'Starting live stacking with reference: .../audit_L_024.fits' then 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars'. Root cause verified in source exactly as stated: fits.rs:322-365 encodes with to_le_bytes for BITPIX 16/32/-32/-64 while bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:1530-1561 image_data_to_linear_f64 decodes U16/U32/F32/F64 with from_be_bytes. Arithmetic matches the symptom: background 440 ADU = 0x01B8 → LE [B8,01] → BE read 0xB801 = 47105; a 40614 ADU star = 0x9EA6 → [A6,9E] → 0xA69E = 42654, i.e. stars end up DARKER than the swapped background, hence 0 detections. Independent pixel check of audit_L_024.fits: median 420, MAD-sigma 22.2, 40 peaks, max 40916. Location correct, with one addition for the fixer: image_data_to_linear_f64 has a SECOND caller, api_compute_fits_quality_maps at imaging.rs:2235, so the same byte-swap corrupts the FITS quality-map endpoint too — wider blast radius than the finding states.

title: Observing Alerts reports a First Light detection's brightness CHANGE as its apparent magnitude, so a self-discovered transient is announced as 'mag 2.4  NAKED EYE'
what_happened: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts renders the First Light detection as 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova - Unconfirmed - possible new transient / 13h 29m 52s +47 11' 43" / mag 2.4 [NAKED EYE]'. The detection row has delta_mag = -2.35 (a brightness CHANGE in magnitudes relative to the atlas template) and no photometric zero point anywhere in the pipeline -- there is no apparent magnitude for this object at all. transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 sets `magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs()`, and the card at transient_card.dart:581 then buckets `magnitude <= 6.0` as NAKED EYE, <= 10 BINOCULAR, <= 14 SMALL SCOPE. Because a difference-image delta magnitude of more than ~6 is essentially impossible, EVERY First Light self-discovery that has a measured delta is announced as a naked-eye or binocular object. The app is telling the user they have found a magnitude-2.4 supernova -- brighter than Polaris, and the brightest supernova in recorded history.
expected: Do not populate the alert's apparent-magnitude field from a delta magnitude. Either leave magnitude null (the card already handles a null magnitude by omitting the chip) and show the delta separately as 'Δ2.35 mag', or compute a real apparent magnitude from a photometric zero point when one exists. The NAKED EYE / BINOCULAR / SMALL SCOPE bucketing must never run on a delta.
repro: 1. Insert a transient_detections row with kind='newSource', delta_mag=-2.35, snr=18.4, reviewed=1. 2. Restart the app. 3. Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts. 4. Read the chip on the alert card.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-21.png: green chip 'mag 2.4  NAKED EYE' next to a card titled 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova'. DB: select id,kind,delta_mag,snr,fwhm from transient_detections -> 1|newSource|-2.35|18.4|2.41. There is no apparent-magnitude column on the table at all and photometric_transforms is empty, so 2.4 cannot be an apparent magnitude by construction.
proposed_fix: Add a distinct deltaMag field to TransientAlert and leave `magnitude` null for First Light detections; render 'Δ 2.35 mag brighter' instead of 'mag 2.4', and suppress the brightness bucket entirely when only a delta is known.
verdict_reasoning: Code, data and UI all check out. transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 is exactly 'final magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs();' and is passed straight into TransientAlert.magnitude, the apparent-magnitude field every alert surface consumes. transient_card.dart:580-588 _getBrightnessInfo buckets magnitude<=6 NAKED EYE / <=10 BINOCULAR / <=14 SMALL SCOPE, called at :532 and rendered as 'mag ${magnitude.toStringAsFixed(1)}' at :553. DB: transient_detections has exactly one row, kind=newSource delta_mag=-2.35 snr=18.4, and the table has no apparent-magnitude column at all, so 2.4 cannot be an apparent magnitude by construction. Confirmed live on my own profile: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts renders 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova - Unconfirmed — possible new transient / mag 2.4 / NAKED EYE'. Because a difference-image delta larger than ~6 mag is essentially impossible, every First Light self-discovery with a measured delta is bucketed NAKED EYE or BINOCULAR. Cited file:line is precise.

title: The photometry 'Uncertainty' column mixes two units: magnitudes for target/check rows and raw ADU flux noise for every comparison-star row, ~3 million times larger
what_happened: Analytics > Science > (export hub) > Photometry Measurements > CSV exports 495 rows with columns ... SNR, Uncertainty ... For target and check rows Uncertainty is a magnitude sigma (0.00054-0.00071 across all 198 such rows). For every one of the 297 comparison rows it is instead the flux noise in ADU (1912.7-2211.8). The identity is exact, not approximate: `select max(abs(uncertainty - flux/snr)) from photometry_measurements where role='comparison'` returns 0.0. So one column, in the database and in the CSV a user hands to AAVSO or plots error bars from, carries two physical quantities that differ by a factor of about 3.4 million, with no unit column to tell them apart.
expected: Uncertainty must be a magnitude sigma for every row. A comparison star's uncertainty is 1.0857/SNR (or the same variance-propagated sigma the check star already gets); the ADU flux noise, if it is wanted, belongs in a separate `flux_uncertainty` column with its own header.
repro: 1. Run a science session so photometry_measurements is populated (495 rows here). 2. Analytics > Science > toolbar database icon > Photometry Measurements > CSV. 3. Open the CSV: target/check rows have Uncertainty ~6e-4, comparison rows ~2.1e3. 4. Confirm in the DB: select role,count(*),min(uncertainty),max(uncertainty),max(abs(uncertainty-flux/snr)) from photometry_measurements group by role -> check|99|0.00056|0.00071|2354.4, comparison|297|1912.7|2211.8|0.0, target|99|0.00054|0.00068|2478.3.
evidence: Exported file /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-16-14.csv, e.g. image 100: target_primary flux 4629522 snr 2119.58 unc 0.000597 / comparison_2 flux 4506308 snr 2090.34 unc 2155.777 where flux/snr = 2155.777. Source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/science_processing_service/private_helpers.dart:465-471 `uncertainty: drift.Value<double?>(checkUncertainty ?? star.flux / (star.snr...))`.
proposed_fix: Replace the `?? star.flux / star.snr` fallback with a magnitude sigma (1.0857 / snr). Add a schema-level unit note and a test asserting every uncertainty in the table is < 1.0 magnitude.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently. private_helpers.dart:465-471 is exactly as cited: uncertainty: drift.Value<double?>(checkUncertainty ?? star.flux / (star.snr.isFinite ? star.snr.clamp(1.0,1e6).toDouble() : 1.0)). checkUncertainty is only non-null on the isCheck branch where it is 1.0857*sqrt(variance) — a magnitude sigma (lines 442-450) — so every comparison row falls through to flux/SNR, which is ADU flux noise. Verified in the scratch DB: group by role gives check|99|5.6e-4|7.1e-4, comparison|297|1912.68|2211.76 with max(abs(uncertainty - flux/snr)) = 0.0 exactly, target|99|5.4e-4|6.8e-4. Verified in the exported CSV /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-16-14.csv: header 'Session ID,Image ID,Object ID,Role,X,Y,Flux,Differential Magnitude,SNR,Uncertainty,Is Outlier,Timestamp', column 10 is ~6e-4 for target/check and ~2e3 for comparison. One column, two physical quantities differing by ~3.4 million, no unit column. file:line correct.
